q: Orders banning or blacklisting a firm for supply of stores to the Railways take effect:

options.A: Only in the single depot which issued the orders
options.B: For one tender only
options.C: Secretly, without being communicated to any office
options.D: Across the Railways, the orders being circulated to all zonal railways

q: A petty and urgent requirement of stores of small value is to be met by local purchase. Under this mode of purchase:

options.A: A Spot Purchase Committee inspects the material available in the market and purchases it on the spot at a reasonable rate
options.B: The storekeeper alone purchases from any shop without keeping any record
options.C: Tenders are invited through press advertisement
options.D: The material is borrowed permanently from another depot

q: The quantity required against a tender is very large and is also required urgently, and the Tender Committee recommends splitting of the order. Splitting of the order means:

options.A: Dividing the tender notice into two advertisements
options.B: Cancelling the tender and inviting two separate tenders
options.C: Placing the order partly with the lowest tenderer and partly with another acceptable tenderer who agrees to match the lowest rate, so that the full quantity is secured in time
options.D: Placing the order on the highest tenderer alone

q: The distinction between a definite quantity contract and a rate (running) contract in stores purchase is that:

options.A: A definite quantity contract carries no fixed rate
options.B: A definite quantity contract is for a specified definite quantity at the contracted rate, whereas a rate contract is for supplies on demand without a commitment as to the total quantity
options.C: A definite quantity contract is used only for imported stores
options.D: A rate contract is used only for the sale of scrap

q: For certain common items, rate contracts are concluded centrally by the Railway Board. A zonal railway obtains its supplies of such items by:

options.A: Inviting fresh tenders for every requirement
options.B: Purchasing from the open market at market rates
options.C: Manufacturing the items in railway workshops only
options.D: Placing supply orders on the firms against the Railway Board rate contract

q: An item is to be stocked in a depot for the first time. Before it is stocked, it is necessary to:

options.A: Allot it a PL number and fix its AAC and stock limits, so that it can be stocked and accounted for
options.B: Obtain a Proprietary Article Certificate for the item
options.C: Sell off the entire old stock of the depot
options.D: Hold an e-auction for its purchase

q: An item is no longer required to be stocked because the equipment using it has been withdrawn. After review, the correct treatment is that the item is:

options.A: Continued in the Priced Vocabulary for ever without any change
options.B: Transferred compulsorily to every other depot
options.C: Deleted from the stock list and Priced Vocabulary, the balance stock held being dealt with as surplus
options.D: Issued free of cost to the depot staff

q: Items which show no issues over a long period are brought out in periodical non-moving lists mainly so that:

options.A: Their book rates can be doubled
options.B: Their continued retention can be reviewed and surplus or obsolete stock can be declared and disposed of
options.C: They can be transferred to the personal custody of the storekeeper
options.D: Fresh purchase orders can be placed for them at once

q: A lot of scrap offered in an e-auction remains unsold. The lot is ordinarily:

options.A: Destroyed at the depot immediately after the auction
options.B: Delivered free of cost to the highest bidder of another lot
options.C: Taken back into the priced stock as serviceable stores
options.D: Re-offered in a subsequent auction, if necessary after revising the reserve price with the approval of the competent authority

q: Before scrap arising in depots is offered for sale by e-auction, it is sorted and segregated according to its description and nature mainly in order to:

options.A: Obtain better realisation in the auction
options.B: Increase its weight before sale
options.C: Reduce its book value in the accounts
options.D: Delay its disposal as long as possible

q: A scrap lot has been knocked down to a purchaser who has paid for it and now presents himself at the depot to take the material away. At the time of taking delivery, the purchaser is required to:

options.A: Get the material transported to his premises free of cost by the Railway
options.B: Wait until the next auction is held by the depot
options.C: Load and remove the material at his own cost within the stipulated delivery period
options.D: Take delivery at the premises of the original supplier of the stores

q: A depot holds paints and rubber goods which have a limited shelf life. To prevent deterioration and loss, issues of such stores from stock are ordinarily made:

options.A: At random from any bin in the ward
options.B: From the latest stock first, keeping the old stock in reserve
options.C: Only against cash payment by the consuming department
options.D: On the first-in-first-out basis, the oldest stock being issued first so that it is consumed before its shelf life expires

q: Petrol, oils and paints, being inflammable in nature, are stored in a depot:

options.A: Along with the general stores in any ward of the depot
options.B: Separately, in specially protected accommodation away from other stores
options.C: In the open yard without any protection
options.D: In the office room of the depot

q: Copper and brass fittings held in a depot are valuable items prone to pilferage. Such attractive stores are kept:

options.A: Under special lock and key, with restricted access
options.B: On open racks accessible to all depot staff
options.C: In the scrap yard along with condemned stores
options.D: Permanently in the custody of the user departments

q: Stores are stolen from a depot. Besides reporting the matter to the departmental authorities, the theft is reported to:

options.A: The local press
options.B: The firm which supplied the stores
options.C: The RPF or Police, for investigation
options.D: The Stores Tender Committee

q: Input tax credit of the GST paid on a stores purchase is available to the Railway. In that situation, the GST amount is:

options.A: Added in full to the book value of the stores in the Priced Stores Ledger
options.B: Recovered from the depot storekeeper
options.C: Treated as part of the inventory carrying cost of the item
options.D: Not added to the cost of the stores, the credit being accounted for separately

q: Stores manufactured in a railway workshop are transferred to a stores depot. They are taken into stock at:

options.A: The prevailing market price of similar material
options.B: The cost of manufacture, comprising material, labour and on-cost, as worked out through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: The cost of the raw material alone
options.D: A nominal value of one rupee per item

q: Stores are issued from a depot for a deposit work executed by the Railway on behalf of an outside party at the cost of that party. The cost of such stores is:

options.A: Charged to the deposit work, being recoverable from the party on whose behalf the work is executed
options.B: Borne by the Railway and charged to its ordinary revenue
options.C: Issued free of cost without any accountal
options.D: Adjusted through the Sales Suspense Account in all cases

q: A Letter of Credit has been opened for imported stores. Payment to the foreign supplier under the Letter of Credit is made:

options.A: Only after the material has been received and verified in the Indian depot
options.B: In cash to the agent of the supplier at the Indian port
options.C: Against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents through the bank, and not on physical receipt of the material in India
options.D: Only after the close of the financial year in which the order was placed

q: Stores are purchased on F.O.R. destination terms and a shortage occurs in transit before delivery at the destination depot. The shortage in transit is:

options.A: Borne by the Railway from the moment of despatch by the supplier
options.B: Borne personally by the depot storekeeper
options.C: Written off without any claim on anybody
options.D: The responsibility of the supplier, the transit risk remaining his until the material is delivered and accepted at destination

q: In a high-value stores procurement, an Integrity Pact is signed between the Railway and the bidders. The working of the pact is overseen by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper of the consignee depot
options.B: The lowest tenderer in the tender
options.C: Independent External Monitors
options.D: The Inspector of Stores Accounts

q: A supplier fails to supply stores because an earthquake destroys his factory and claims relief under the force majeure clause of the contract. A second supplier claims the same relief merely because market prices of raw material have risen. The correct position is that:

options.A: Both suppliers are entitled to relief under the clause
options.B: Neither supplier is entitled to relief under the clause
options.C: Only the supplier facing rising prices is entitled to relief
options.D: Only the supplier affected by the event beyond his control is entitled to relief, a rise in market prices being an ordinary business risk

q: Midway through a stores contract, the contractor sublets the entire contract to another firm, merely sending an intimation to the depot. Under the IRS Conditions of Contract, this subletting is:

options.A: Valid, as intimation to the depot is sufficient
options.B: Not permissible, as a contractor shall not assign or sublet the contract or any part of it without the written consent of the Railway
options.C: Valid, provided the other firm is registered with the Railways
options.D: Valid, provided the contractor remains responsible for the supplies

q: A bidder from a country sharing a land border with India participates in a stores tender but is not registered with the Registration Committee set up by the DPIIT. Under Rule 144(xi) of the General Financial Rules, the bidder is:

options.A: Eligible, registration being required only after the tender is accepted
options.B: Not eligible to participate in the tender
options.C: Eligible, if it is exempted from payment of earnest money
options.D: Eligible, if the depot officer inviting the tender approves its participation

q: A firm tries to submit its e-bid for stores on IREPS a few minutes after the due date and time fixed for submission of bids. In this situation:

options.A: The bid cannot be submitted, as the system automatically closes bid submission at the stipulated time
options.B: The bid is accepted on payment of a late fee by the firm
options.C: The bid is accepted with the approval of the Tender Committee
options.D: The bid is kept pending and treated as an unsolicited offer

q: Before a firm can submit an e-tender for stores on the IREPS portal, it is required to have:

options.A: A seller registration on the GeM portal only
options.B: A valid Digital Signature Certificate
options.C: An ISO certification for its products
options.D: A bank guarantee from a nationalised bank

q: Besides being published on the IREPS portal, railway stores tenders are also published on the:

options.A: Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal
options.B: Website of the lowest tenderer
options.C: Notice board of the consignee depot only
options.D: GeM portal only

q: A firm pays the prescribed price for the tender documents of a stores tender, but its tender is ultimately not accepted. The price paid by the firm for the tender documents is:

options.A: Refunded to the firm in full
options.B: Adjusted against the earnest money deposit of the firm
options.C: Not refundable, whether or not the firm submits a tender
options.D: Refunded only if the tender is discharged without acceptance

q: On the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), the consignee has generated the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) for goods received and accepted. Payment to the GeM seller is required to be made within:

options.A: 30 days of the generation of the CRAC
options.B: 45 days of the generation of the CRAC
options.C: 15 days of the generation of the CRAC
options.D: 10 days of the generation of the CRAC

q: In the e-auction of scrap conducted on IREPS, a bidder who wishes to better the current highest bid for a lot must ensure that his bid:

options.A: Is equal to the reserve price of the lot
options.B: Exceeds the previous highest bid at least by the bid increment specified for the lot
options.C: Is accompanied by a fresh earnest money deposit
options.D: Is approved in advance by the Tender Committee

q: Before a lot of scrap is put up for e-auction, a reserve price is fixed for it. The effect of the reserve price is that the lot is:

options.A: Ordinarily not sold below that price without the approval of the competent authority
options.B: Sold at that price to the first bidder who registers for the auction
options.C: Offered first to the firm which originally supplied the stores
options.D: Withdrawn from the auction if the first bid equals that price

q: After purchasing a lot of scrap in an e-auction, a purchaser complains that some pieces in the lot are bent and worn, and demands a reduction in the price on that account. The correct position under the conditions of sale is that:

options.A: The price is reduced in proportion to the damaged pieces in the lot
options.B: The purchaser may return the damaged pieces and take a refund for them
options.C: No such claim lies, as scrap lots are sold on an 'as is where is' basis and bidders are given an opportunity to inspect the lots before bidding
options.D: The lot is re-auctioned and the purchaser is refunded his full payment

q: A lot of scrap is knocked down in an e-auction at a certain bid price. The taxes and duties leviable on the sale are payable:

options.A: By the Railway out of the bid price realised
options.B: By the stores depot conducting the auction
options.C: Equally by the Railway and the purchaser
options.D: By the purchaser, in addition to the bid price

q: A lot of scrap which is sold by weight is ready for delivery to the purchaser. Delivery of such a lot is given:

options.A: On the basis of the purchaser's own estimate of its weight
options.B: Without any weighment, on a lump-sum basis
options.C: After weighment on a weighbridge, in the presence of the purchaser or his representative
options.D: After weighment at the works of the firm which originally supplied the stores

q: A purchaser of scrap has paid the full sale value of a lot purchased by him in an e-auction. Delivery of the material to him is authorised by the depot through:

options.A: A delivery order
options.B: A fresh purchase order placed on the purchaser
options.C: A stock sheet prepared by the stock verifier
options.D: A tender notice issued by the depot

q: Stores issued from a depot, and scrap sold to a purchaser, are ready to be taken out of the depot premises. Material can be taken out of a stores depot only against:

options.A: A verbal permission given by any depot official
options.B: A gate pass issued on the basis of the issue note or delivery order, as the case may be
options.C: A copy of the tender notice for the item
options.D: The bin card maintained at the bin

q: Material from all sources — purchases, workshop manufacture, transfers from other depots and returns from departments — is received at a stores depot. In the first instance, all such material received is entered by the depot in the:

options.A: Priced Stores Ledger
options.B: Bin Card
options.C: Daily Receipt Register
options.D: Issue Register

q: During stock verification of an item, the quantity actually found in the depot on physical verification, as distinct from the balance shown in the records, is referred to as the:

options.A: Book balance of the item
options.B: Ledger balance of the item
options.C: Bin balance of the item
options.D: Ground balance of the item

q: Tools and plant issued to a department for use remain railway property, are accountable numerically and are required to be returned after use. Such returnable items are borne on the:

options.A: Dead Stock Register
options.B: Priced Stores Ledger
options.C: Bin Card
options.D: Stores Monthly Summary

q: Stores are issued from a depot to a railway workshop for use on a job under manufacture or repair in the workshop. At the time of issue, the value of such stores is initially debited to:

options.A: Purchase Suspense
options.B: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Sales Suspense

q: Stores are issued from a depot to another railway, to an outside department or to a firm, and their value is awaiting final adjustment or recovery. Pending such adjustment, the value is accommodated under the:

options.A: Stores Miscellaneous Suspense head
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: Sales Suspense head
options.D: Traffic Suspense head

q: During stock verification, a shortage of an item is found in one ward of a depot, while an excess of the same item is found in another ward of the same depot. The correct treatment of these differences is that:

options.A: The excess is set off against the shortage and only the net difference is recorded
options.B: The shortage is ignored, since the total depot stock of the item is correct
options.C: The excess is treated as the personal property of the stockholder of that ward
options.D: Each difference is brought on record and adjusted separately through its own stock sheet, the shortage in one ward not being set off against the excess in another ward

q: On completion of stock verification of an item, the stockholder signs the stock sheet recording the difference between the physical and the book balances. By this signature, the stockholder signifies that:

options.A: He has seen and noted the difference recorded in the stock sheet
options.B: He admits personal liability for the difference in all cases
options.C: He agrees to make good the shortage from his pay immediately
options.D: He certifies that the book balance of the item was correct

q: Equipment ordered on a supplier is still under manufacture at his works, and the purchase order provides for inspection at different points during the process of manufacture itself. Such inspection carried out in stages during manufacture is known as:

options.A: Surprise inspection
options.B: Post-delivery inspection
options.C: Stage inspection
options.D: Stock verification

q: A Tender Accepting Authority accepts a tenderer's offer subject to a qualification which changes one of the conditions of the offer. In law, the effect of such a qualified acceptance is that:

options.A: A contract is concluded on the terms of the original offer
options.B: It amounts to a counter-offer and does not by itself conclude a contract, a contract being concluded only on absolute and unqualified acceptance of the offer
options.C: A contract is concluded on the terms imposed by the Railway alone
options.D: The tender itself stands cancelled automatically

q: A supplier offers quantity discounts on an item, the unit price falling as the quantity ordered increases. The decision whether to avail of the discount by ordering a larger quantity is taken by:

options.A: Always accepting the largest quantity, as its unit price is the lowest
options.B: Comparing only the ordering cost at each quantity
options.C: Comparing only the carrying cost at each quantity
options.D: Comparing the total cost — purchase cost, ordering cost and carrying cost — at the Economic Order Quantity and at each price-break quantity

q: A purchase office groups stores items according to whether they are obtained from Government sources, ordinary trade sources, local sources or foreign sources, for purposes of inventory control. This classification is made under:

options.A: GOLF analysis
options.B: ABC analysis
options.C: VED analysis
options.D: FSN analysis

q: A purchase clerk needs the Stores Code rule on inviting and accepting stores tenders, while a depot officer needs the rule on custody of stores and depot accounts. In the Indian Railway Stores Code, issued in two volumes, they will find these rules respectively in:

options.A: Volume II for both subjects
options.B: Volume I for both subjects
options.C: Volume I, which deals mainly with purchase of stores, and Volume II, which deals with depot working, custody and accounts of stores
options.D: Volume II, which deals mainly with purchase of stores, and Volume I, which deals with depot working, custody and accounts of stores

q: The same stores item is held in the depots of two different zonal railways. Regarding the book (issue) rate of the item on the two railways, the correct position is that the rate:

options.A: Must be identical on all railways, being fixed by the Railway Board
options.B: Is uniform within a railway, but may differ from one railway to another
options.C: Differs from depot to depot even within the same railway
options.D: Is fixed separately by each depot for its own stock

q: Two tenderers quote for the same stores item: one quotes a lower ex-works price but high freight to destination, while the other quotes a higher ex-works price with delivery at destination. For evaluating the tenders, the rates are compared on the basis of:

options.A: The ex-works price quoted by the tenderers only
options.B: The last accepted rate for the item
options.C: The estimated rate prepared by the purchase office
options.D: The total price payable by the Railway at destination, including freight, taxes and duties
